verdicts.description: An array of verdicts, exactly one object per evaluated paper.

reasoning.description: Brief reasoning, 1-3 sentences. Start by identifying the DV (LHS) of the main regression(s) and whether it is logged. Note any log-on-RHS terms separately — those do NOT make this log-DV.

is_empirical.description: Does this paper estimate regressions on real data? 'no' = pure theory/methodology/conceptual; 'partial' = mostly theory with brief empirical illustration; 'yes' = main contribution includes empirical estimation. If 'no', log_dv_likely MUST be 'no' and transformation MUST be 'none'.

log_dv_likely.description: Is the DEPENDENT variable (LHS) logged or Poisson-modeled? 'yes' requires DIRECT textual evidence in the body (log(Y) equation, table header naming a logged outcome, explicit prose). Inference from 'this outcome is conventionally logged in the literature' or back-calculation from coefficient interpretation, WITHOUT textual markers, = 'speculative', NOT 'yes'. Log-transforms on the RHS as controls do NOT count.

transformation.description: Which specific transformation is on the LHS of the main regression? Specific values (log/log1p/arcsinh/poisson) require DIRECT textual evidence. When log_dv_likely='speculative' (inferred from literature norms), prefer 'unclear' over guessing a specific transformation.

panel.description: STRICTLY about TIME. SAME units observed for the DV at ≥2 distinct TIME periods (longitudinal), supporting entity AND time fixed effects that are used in the regression. No entity → repeated_cross_section. No time → see `hd_fe` for high-dimensional FE without time.

repeated_cross_section.description: DIFFERENT samples drawn from the same population at ≥2 distinct time periods (separate cohorts/waves, no within-unit tracking). E.g., separate RCTs in different years on different participants is repeated cross-section, not panel. Requires the DV to be measured at multiple time periods; a single time-point study is neither.

regression_discontinuity.description: Uses Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD, cutoffs, running variables).

experimental.description: Uses clear randomization methods (RCTs, lab experiments, field experiments, lotteries, etc).

multiarm_treatment.description: THREE OR MORE distinct treatment arms compared (e.g., "cash arm vs employment arm vs control"; "letter A vs letter B vs letter C").

lots_of_controls.description: Explicitly relies on a rich set of covariates. Tracks regular covariates and fixed-count FE (region, industry — bounded by the number of regions/industries, not by N). DOES NOT include high-dimensional sample-growing FE — those go in `hd_fe`.

hd_fe.description: High-dimensional fixed effects whose count grows with the sample (individual/worker/firm/household/match FE, AKM-style two-way FE).

costly_intervention.description: Evaluates an intervention or policy that involves significant financial, time, or resource costs per subject treated.

heterogeneous_effects.description: A dedicated subgroup analysis across subjects, causal forests, or treatment×covariate interactions with noticeable differences.

dummy_outcome.description: Uses a binary/dummy dependent variable (e.g., probability models, extensive margin participation).

dummy_treatment.description: Uses a binary/dummy independent variable (e.g., policy adoption, program participation, gender as a main variable of interest).

other_methods.description: Use this field to list other notable method features if any (list of short keywords).

data_source.description: Identify all origins of the data used in the empirical analysis. Select ALL that apply from the list. If no data analysis, leave empty [].
